name: Dakota
notes: Dakota (Dakȟótiyapi), Siouan (Dakotan branch, sister to Lakota). Five oral vowels /a e i o u/ and three nasal vowels /ã ĩ ũ/, written with the tilde. Obstruents show a three-way (in places four-way) laryngeal contrast: plain voiceless unaspirated (p t k), h-aspirated (ph th kh, čh), a second 'fricated'/velar-released aspirated series marked with caron-h (pȟ tȟ kȟ, phonetically a stop with audible frication [pˣ tˣ kˣ]), and ejectives marked with an apostrophe (pʼ tʼ kʼ čʼ). A separate plain-voiced series (b d g) also occurs, mostly in loanwords and certain grammatical contexts. ⟨ȟ⟩ alone is the voiceless uvular fricative /χ/ (with ejective ȟʼ); its voiced counterpart is ⟨ǧ⟩ /ʁ/. ⟨'⟩ standing alone is the glottal stop /ʔ/. This is the standard Dakota practical orthography as used in modern pedagogical and dictionary sources; vowel length is not consistently marked and is therefore not represented here.
